messages:
maya (eng-runtime): Heads-up — noticed a ~15% token-level latency bump on prod around 08:10-08:18 UTC. P95 up, p99 also nudging. Suspect kernel fallback churn + kv cache miss spike.

liam (eng-runtime): ugh. any deploys in that window?

deploy-bot: deploy completed by noah at 2026-03-15T08:05:12Z — service: runtime-kit — version: v2.14.3 — cfg: kernel-selector=v2

maya (eng-runtime): thanks. timeline aligns (deploy 08:05 then spike 08:10). Kernel-selector v2 rolled at that deploy.

tom (eng-sre): can you paste the token-latency query you used? will pull related SLI graphs.

maya (eng-runtime): here's the quick PromQL I ran in Grafana: 

  sum(rate(token_latency_ms_bucket{env="prod"}[5m])) by (le,route)

then derive p95/p99 from buckets. Also looked at kv_cache_hit_rate: 

  increase(kv_cache_misses_total{env="prod"}[5m]) / increase(kv_cache_lookups_total{env="prod"}[5m])

both show miss rate jump from 4% -> 18% during spike.

eva (observability): adding panels to the per-route dashboard now: token p50/p95/p99, kv-miss-rate, kernel-fallback-rate, batch-size distribution. Will link when ready.

liam (eng-runtime): my profiling trace (local capture of a reproduced request) shows that when kernel-selector can't find a warmed kernel it falls back to generic GPU kernel which has ~2-3x per-token cost for short sequences. Fallback count spiked.

noah (eng-platform): kernel warmup job should have pre-warmed common variants — v2 changed the warming heuristic (now warms by model id only, not shape). Could be the culprit.

tom (eng-sre): ops question: are we paging on burn-rate or absolute latency? Current alert rules: 

  - name: RuntimeLatencyBurnRate
    expr: runtime_latency_burn_rate{env="prod"} > 2
    for: 10m
    labels: {severity: page}

that's pretty strict. We didn't get a page — only internal slack alerts.

maya (eng-runtime): can we quickly rollback kernel-selector to v1? That would verify. But I'd rather try a config flip: revert warmup heuristic change (shape-less warming) and increase prewarm concurrency for top-10 routes.

liam (eng-runtime): agree on config flip first. Rolling back code is heavier. I can push a config change to increase warmup parallelism + re-enable shape-based warming.

noah (eng-platform): I'll open a quick rollout: change cfg kernel-warmup.strategy=shape-and-model and kernel-warmup.parallelism=8. Will canary to 5% of requests for 10m.

eva (observability): FYI I've created short-lived anomaly alert (noise suppression): 

  - name: TokenLatencyAnomaly
    expr: increase(token_latency_ms_sum{env="prod"}[5m]) / increase(token_latency_ms_count{env="prod"}[5m]) > (avg_over_time(token_latency_ms_avg{env="prod"}[1h]) * 1.3)
    for: 5m
    labels: {severity: ticket}

this will create a ticket if baseline relative increases exceed 30% for 5m.

tom (eng-sre): Good. For paging thresholds we should use burn-rate of 3 over 5m for paging; 2 over 15m for ops ticket. Right now paging at 2 for 10m seems to flip too often for transient rollout noise.

maya (eng-runtime): +1 to raising page threshold, but let's keep route-specific exceptions for high-SLA customers (route: /customer/x). Those should remain at burn-rate 1.5.

liam (eng-runtime): also raising batching wait cap from 5ms -> 2ms for latency-sensitive routes helped before. Maybe kernel-selector v2 has interaction where larger batches trigger falls back due to memory layout mismatch. I'll instrument batch_size by kernel_variant.

noah (eng-platform): I've scheduled the canary change — applying at 08:45 UTC. Will monitor the canary and revert automatically if kernel_fallback_rate > 1% or token_p95 increases > 10% in canary.

maya (eng-runtime): action items:
- liam: add kernel_variant label to batching histogram + ship metric (5m)
- eva: add the new panels and wire the TokenLatencyAnomaly alert into ops-tickets channel
- noah: roll the warmup config canary 5% now; timeline 10m, auto-revert thresholds as above
- tom: prepare updated paging thresholds PR (pages: burn-rate >=3 for global, exceptions per-route)

liam (eng-runtime): I'll also add a short-term mitigation: when kernel_fallback_rate > 0.5% we'll reduce max_batch_bytes for affected pool to avoid memory-layout fallbacks. Quick config patch.

tom (eng-sre): ack. Please paste the PR links here when ready. If we still see P99 degradation after canary, we'll do a rollback.

maya (eng-runtime): thanks all. Keep notes in the incident channel if it escalates. For now, looks like config warmup + batching tweak should remove the regression.

noah (eng-platform): canary started at 08:45:12Z — monitoring...

eva (observability): dashboards updated: https://grafana.internal/r/abcd1234/runtime-token-latency (new panels at top).

maya (eng-runtime): closing loop: after canary warmup change p95 returned to baseline in canary and global after gradual roll-out. Kernel_fallback_rate dropped from 1.9% -> 0.2%. KV-miss rate also returned to ~5%. Leaving follow-ups: add automated warmup audit and a per-deploy gating check for kernel_warmup_coverage.

liam (eng-runtime): will post the metric PR and a short runbook paragraph for oncall.

tom (eng-sre): nice work. marking this as resolved unless anyone objects. :thumbsup:
